note: Short quotations from published extension and university sources, copied word for word from documents opened on the compile date. A pin with no note has a gap listed under 'gaps' saying what could not be read. Nothing here is advice written by this app.

notes.quote: Halophytes such as cotton are among the most tolerant crops that give economic returns and provide a stable income for most Westside growers, however in many areas do not escape the yield losses associated with salinity and poor drainage.
notes.by: Daniel Munk, UC Cooperative Extension, Fresno County
notes.source: Contrasting Irrigation Application Methods for Drainage Reduction and Soil Salinity Management (project summary, funded 2001-2002 by The Prosser Trust), Executive Summary
notes.limits: Written about the west side of the San Joaquin Valley. The Fresno demo pin is a point in the region and may not sit on the west side. It is an early-2000s project summary, not current guidance.

notes.quote: the majority of irrigation losses to deep percolation occur during the singular pre-irrigation event where high soil infiltrations rates cause an over application of irrigation water.
notes.by: Daniel Munk, UC Cooperative Extension, Fresno County, reporting the Committee of Consultants on Drainage Water Reduction (1988)
notes.source: Contrasting Irrigation Application Methods for Drainage Reduction and Soil Salinity Management (project summary, funded 2001-2002 by The Prosser Trust), Executive Summary
notes.limits: A 1988 finding repeated in an early-2000s project summary for the west side of the San Joaquin Valley. It describes where water was lost then, not what happens on this field now.

notes.quote: nutrient removal should not be the sole basis for nutrient application and fertilization rates.
notes.by: Roberts, Kirkpatrick, Slaton and Norman, University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture
notes.source: Estimating Nutrient Removal for Row Crops Grown in Arkansas, FSA2176 (2015), page 1
notes.limits: An Arkansas publication. It is the same document the app's crop-removal figures come from, so it states the limit of those figures.

notes.quote: The best and most accurate way to determine nutrient removal is to collect representative grain samples and have them analyzed.
notes.by: Roberts, Kirkpatrick, Slaton and Norman, University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture
notes.source: Estimating Nutrient Removal for Row Crops Grown in Arkansas, FSA2176 (2015), page 3
notes.limits: An Arkansas publication about grain crops.

gaps.text: No Delta-specific local note is shown. The UC Delta Crops Resource Management pages and a Delta Protection Commission page returned 'access denied' (HTTP 403) when opened on 2026-11-15, so nothing from them was read or used.
Only the two Fresno County notes above were readable. No current UC irrigation or nutrient guidance for cotton or other catalog crops was opened.

No Punjab note is shown. The copy of a 2009 sub-soil water Act that could be opened was the Haryana Act, a different state, so it was not used, and the Punjab Act and Punjab Agricultural University pages could not be opened (access denied or not found) on 2026-11-15.
